Consult Summary:
19-year-old female university student with 1-week history of dysuria, urinary frequency, pink-tinged urine, and suprapubic ache. Clinical impression is uncomplicated lower urinary tract infection; urine sample and empiric oral antibiotics arranged. 

Problem List:

Issue 1: Dysuria / Suspected uncomplicated cystitis (UTI)
- Onset just under 1 week; burning/stinging on micturition, increased urinary frequency, pink urine noted today, suprapubic aching worse during voiding.
- Associated symptoms: denies flank/back pain, nausea, vomiting, fever, vaginal discharge.
- Review of systems: bowels unchanged (known IBS); no systemic symptoms.
- Sexual history: sexually active with long-term partner, on combined OCP, no condom use; last unprotected intercourse 1–2 weeks ago; last menstrual period 2 weeks ago.
- Examination: none performed; no vitals documented.
- Impression: Likely uncomplicated lower UTI; pregnancy considered but low suspicion at present.

Issue 2: Irritable Bowel Syndrome (pre-existing)
- Long-standing variable stool frequency/consistency; currently baseline, no new gastrointestinal symptoms.
- Medication: Mebeverine (dose/route/frequency not documented).

Issue 3: Recreational cannabis use (single episode)
- Smoked cannabis once ~1.5 weeks ago at party; no ongoing use planned.
- Counseled to avoid future use.

Medications:
- Combined oral contraceptive pill (specific brand/dose not documented).
- Mebeverine (dose/route/frequency not documented).

Allergies:
- Clindamycin – adverse reaction (details not documented).

Past Medical History:
- Irritable Bowel Syndrome.

Social History:
- Lives in university halls with flatmate; family live outside London.
- Non-smoker of tobacco; occasional social alcohol.
- Single trial of cannabis 1.5 weeks ago.
- Undergraduate English student.

Preventative History:
- No information documented regarding cervical screening, immunizations, STI screening, or other preventive health measures.

Physical Examination:
- No physical exam performed; no vitals recorded.
- Reported absence of fever, flank pain, nausea, or vomiting.

Plan:
- Provide sterile container; patient to drop off mid-stream urine sample for dipstick and culture.
- Start empiric 3-day oral antibiotic: Nitrofurantoin or Trimethoprim (exact agent and dose to be finalized on prescription).
- Encourage adequate oral hydration.
- Analgesia: Paracetamol as needed.
- Safety-net advice: seek urgent review if develops fever, flank/back pain, vomiting, or worsening symptoms.
- Routine follow-up: if no improvement after completed antibiotic course (~1 week) to re-attend for reassessment; consider pregnancy test if symptoms persist.

Quality checks (document_quality):
● Missing expected elements: vital signs, physical examination findings, detailed allergy reaction, complete medication list with doses, vaccination and cervical screening status.
● No internal conflicts identified.
● Transcript quality good; occasional minor hesitations but clinically clear.
